text:
olivia: Heads-up — customer ACC-3345 opened a dispute. They say invoice INV-2026-0887 billed ~4.2M tokens but their dashboard shows ~2.1M. They want a recount + refund. attaching their thread excerpt and invoice link: https://console.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-2026-0887 :eyes:

devon: I pulled the metering export for ACC-3345. Raw usage file (s3://metering/exports/acc-3345/2026-03-16.csv) shows duplicated request_ids for a 20m window starting 2026-03-16T02:10Z. looks like a retry loop from an internal batch job. quick snippet:```sql
SELECT request_id, COUNT(*) as cnt, SUM(token_count) as tokens
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id = 'ACC-3345' AND ts >= '2026-03-16'
GROUP BY request_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 5;```

devon: duplicates account for ~2,031,412 tokens (approx). when deduped dashboard matches ~2.17M. so invoice has double-count for that window.

olivia: thanks. can we confirm how invoice was generated? is it live metering -> billing-pipeline or using precomputed daily aggregates?

devon: Invoice pipeline uses daily-agg tables produced by metering-worker. metering-worker had a bug (missing idempotency key on 2.7.4) that caused replays to create duplicate aggregate rows when a worker restarted. i patched worker to 2.7.5 and replay dedupe logic is enabled. patch deployed at 2026-03-16T03:05Z (ops verified).

ops: confirmed 2.7.5 deployed to prod, replay-dedupe flag true, no new duplicates after 03:05Z. rolling back duplicate rows avoided.

marcus: from finance — we need exact adjustment numbers and GL/revrec notes. please provide: net token overcount, USD equivalent on INV-2026-0887, and suggested accounting entry.

devon: net overcount = 2,031,412 tokens. customer tier rate = $0.0006/token (hosted). adjustment = 2,031,412 * 0.0006 = $1,218.8472 -> round to $1,218.85.

marcus: got it. finance will issue a credit for $1,218.85. Refund method? credit to account or ACH refund?

olivia: customer asked for refund to original payment method. they also said they'd accept account credit if faster.

marcus: we'll issue a credit first (applies immediately to next invoice) and start refund to PM if customer insists. create finance ticket with revrec entry.

olivia: creating support response now. draft: "Hi — we found a duplication in our metering pipeline that double-counted ~2.03M tokens on 2026-03-16. We've corrected the pipeline and removed the duplicate events. We've applied a $1,218.85 credit to your account (visible on next invoice) and initiated a refund if you'd prefer the original payment method. Sorry for the inconvenience." okay? :+1: 

devon: add a short technical note for audit logs: "Root cause: metering-worker v2.7.4 missed idempotency on aggregate writes after restart. Fix: v2.7.5 adds idempotent upsert + replay dedupe job. Duplicate aggregates removed from daily_agg on 2026-03-16T03:10Z."

marcus: finance entry prepared: Adjustment ID ADJ-2026-372, Refund/Credit token adjustment RFD-2026-112 (credit posted), RevRec note: REV-2026-045. GL mapping: debit 4100 (Revenue) $1,218.85, credit 4801 (Deferred Revenue reversal) $1,218.85. Accounting comment: "Metering recount adjustment for ACC-3345 due to duplicate aggregates 2026-03-16."

billing-bot: Payment credit applied to account ACC-3345: amount=1218.85 USD, credit_id=CR-2026-19, effective=2026-03-17.

olivia: sent message to customer with options. they replied: "Thanks — prefer refund to card." I relayed to finance.

marcus: initiated ACH/refund: Refund ID RFD-2026-113 created, status=processing. ETA 3-5 business days. Also added internal memo linking INV-2026-0887, ADJ-2026-372, REV-2026-045.

ops: verifying there are no other affected accounts from the same window. quick query shows 6 accounts had >1 duplicate batch events; only ACC-3345 had billing above threshold and raised dispute. I've queued dedupe and recount jobs for the other 5 and will create a summary report by EOD.

devon: added a small monitoring alert to metering-service: if duplicate request_id rate > 0.1% in a 1h window -> pager to eng-oncall.

olivia: final customer note sent at 2026-03-17T09:12Z: "Refund is processing, you'll see it in 3-5 business days. We've applied a $1,218.85 credit in the meantime. We apologize — we've fixed the root cause and added monitoring. Let us know if you'd like the detailed revrec docs."

marcus: finance closed adjustment ADJ-2026-372 as completed when CR-2026-19 posted. Refund RFD-2026-113 still processing.

olivia: closing thread after ops posts the final summary. thanks team :heart:

ops: summary posted to internal drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/metering/duplicates-2026-03-16-summary.pdf (includes CSVs, query runs, affected accounts list).

devon: note for release/changelog: metering-worker 2.7.5 — idempotent upserts + replay-dedupe. changelog PR #4821.

olivia: resolving. if anything else pops up tag me. :white_check_mark:
